text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chinese President Jiang Zemin said he wanted to see China and the United States seize on a recent improvement in their rocky relationship as a foundation for long-term healthy ties.

- Ousted Cambodian First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh, speaking ahead of a special meeting of Asean foreign ministers in Singapore, urged the regional grouping not to recognise Foreign Minister Ung Huot as his successor.
- Singaporeans and Malaysians who have to commute between the two countries daily to work will soon be issued job identification cards so that they will not be held up at immigration checkpoints.
- Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya left cap in hand for Tokyo, saying he needed at least S$10 billion in standby credit from the IMF and other lenders to ease his country's financial crisis.
- The Regentville condominium was the top-selling private housing project in the second quarter, followed by River Place, Eastpoint Green, The Hillside and The Springbloom.
- China launched an intensive campaign to ease fears over the damaging effect of direct foreign investment on the national economy, and to muffle calls for an investment ceiling for foreign firms.

- Almost two years after the 1995 property curbs on foreign buying, the Malaysian residential property sector is likely to see a slump in transactions if not prices, while the commercial property sector is heading for a shake-out, analysts say.

- Hotel Properties Ltd plans to build up a significant property portfolio in Britian beginning with its first major project -- the Canary Riverside at Canary Wharf in London, being developed for some S$904.7 million.
- Umno Youth regrets the action of an ASEAN member country which sold more than S$279 million of its currency at a time when other countries in the region were facing a fall in currency value.
- Singapore hotels are likely to induce a big yawn with flat or negative earnings growth for the six months ended June 1997, analysts said.
